name: 10-Foot Pole
desc: A long stick — for prodding suspicious flagstones, pit lids, and tripwires from a body-length away. The item every dungeon list forgot to explain.

name: Rope (15 m)
desc: Fifteen metres of cordage. Improves a climb, rigs a haul, ties a prisoner — the multi-tool of the pre-modern kit.

name: Lock Picks
desc: A roll of tension wrenches and picks. Without them, opening a lock is a penalty or flatly impossible; with them it's a skill roll.

name: Torch / Flashlight
desc: Portable light. Removes the crippling penalty of acting blind — at the cost of announcing exactly where you are.

name: Binoculars
desc: Magnified optics. Turns a smudge on the horizon into a Scan roll you can actually make.

name: Climbing Kit
desc: Harness, cams, carabiners, rope. Turns an unclimbable pitch into a hard climb, and a fall into a scare instead of a wound.

name: Medical Kit
desc: Field trauma kit. A PM to First Aid; a fuller surgeon's kit reaches Surgery. Without it, treating a serious wound takes a penalty — see the Fields hierarchy.

name: Toolkit
desc: General mechanical tools. Repair needs the diagnosis *and* the tools; this is the tools. A specialist kit gives more for its one trade.

name: Radio / Comm
desc: Two-way voice at range — the thing that makes split-the-party survivable. Jammable, interceptable, and only as private as its encryption.

name: Datapad
desc: Handheld computer and network terminal. A PM to knowledge lookups, and the doorway to every system worth breaking into. Information-tech runs ahead of the rest of the tech scale.

name: Nightvision Goggles
desc: Light-intensifying or thermal optics — the flashlight's advantage without the flashlight's giveaway. Foiled by total dark (needs IR) or by smoke.

name: Vacc Suit
desc: Sealed pressure suit with hours of air. Turns 'the airlock opened' from a death into an inconvenience; clumsy enough to carry an Agility penalty.

name: Medscanner
desc: Handheld diagnostic — reads vitals, names the injury, guides the treatment. A strong PM to the *diagnosis* half of medicine; you still have to do the fixing.
